correctness.rationale: Exact time-dependent XOR gauge maps every phase matrix to L or F and conjugates the p-step product. Zero defects forbid 01 in the gauge and yield n+2 allowed prefixes. Any F produces a primitive matrix; FL^aF-L^{a+1}F=[[1,a],[0,0]] is entrywise nonnegative and nonzero, giving strict Perron descent to the unique-F product whose spectral radius is (p+sqrt(p^2+4))/2. Trace/determinant prove the zeta formulas and direct enumeration proves multiplicities. All quantifiers p>=1 and n>=0, endpoint conventions and per-time entropy normalization are explicit. Exact integer certificate checks all schedules for p<=7 and directly counts short strings/cycles; finite results are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The searched archive-period literature and indexed semantic results did not state the all-period compatibility-defect dichotomy or the sharp first-positive-entropy bound. The 2013 time-dependent-hole paper studies oscillating geometric intervals with numerical/Ulam approximations; the 2019 full-text stationary-hole paper studies fixed forbidden cylinder unions. Neither entails the schedule-wise extremal Perron product by a stated result. General transfer-matrix theory is background and could make an unindexed equivalent specialization a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family of period-p schedules with identically sized dyadic holes has a complete zero-entropy classification, an exact polynomial-corrected maximal escape law, a forbidden interval of achievable escape rates, and an explicit sharp positive-entropy threshold with unique defect mechanism, multiplicities and periodic zeta functions. These are structural and quantitatively sharp results not supplied by generic transfer-matrix correctness or an isolated finite table.
